mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 10.0% signals a severe labor market contraction, prompting aggressive fiscal stimulus and central bank intervention that boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 10.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based consumer demand contraction, which triggers a flight to quality and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 20-day returns, with the Rank IC falling below 0.05 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a recession (defined by a quarterly GDP decline), a recovery in retail sales (RSAFS) signals the start of a consumer-led economic rebound, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where GDPC1 shows a quarterly decline (recession) and RSAFS rises, the S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing output contraction (INDPRO below 95.0) indicates a supply chain disruption that reduces corporate profits and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 95.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 260.0 (index 1982-1984=100) signals persistent inflationary pressures, leading to expectations of tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 260.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase above 138,000 persons signals a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS exceeds 138,000, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and manufacturing output (INDPRO) indicates a dual demand and supply shock, which amplifies economic uncertainty and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and INDPRO fails to predict negative 60-day returns, with the Rank IC falling below 0.05 over a 2-year rolling window.
